app.title: ADB Service Tool
app.subtitle: Service • Data migration • Diagnostics
tools.title: Platform-tools
tools.missingAdb: 'adb' not found. Install Android platform-tools and add it to PATH, or pick the binary manually.
devices.title: Detected devices
devices.noneHint: Connect the device over USB and enable Developer options → USB debugging. Devices in Fastboot or MTP mode are detected too.
devices.unauthorized: Accept “Allow USB debugging?” on the device screen (tick “Always allow”).
devices.offline: Offline — replug the cable or restart the adb server.
devices.noPermissions: Linux: missing udev rules. Install android-udev and add your user to the adbusers/plugdev group.
devices.mtpHint: MTP mode (files only). Enable USB debugging for full functionality.
info.title: Device information
info.notReadable: This mode can't be read — authorize the device or reconnect it.
pull.title: Pull data from device
pull.expandHint: Expand folders and tick what to copy
push.title: Push files to device
push.empty: Add files or folders to send.
push.pickHint: Click a folder in the tree to use it as destination.
push.skipExisting: Skip files already on the device (resume)
apps.title: App manager
apps.needAdb: The app manager requires a device in ADB mode (Android booted).
apps.debloatInfo: Rootless debloat: “Remove” runs pm uninstall -k --user 0 — the app disappears for the user but stays in the system image and can be brought back with “Restore” (or a factory reset). Packages marked CRITICAL can break the device.
apps.criticalWarn: ⚠ WARNING: the selection contains CRITICAL packages. Removing/disabling them may cause a bootloop, a missing home screen or no cellular network.
apps.confirm.uninstall: Remove the selected apps for the current user? App data is kept (-k) and apps can be restored.
apps.confirm.disable: Freeze (disable) the selected apps? They can be unfrozen at any time.
apps.confirm.clear: Wipe ALL data of the selected apps? This cannot be undone.
reboot.title: Quick reboot
reboot.needDevice: Select a device in ADB, Recovery or Fastboot mode.
reboot.warn: Rebooting interrupts running operations on the device.
reboot.d.edl: Qualcomm Emergency Download — service use only
reboot.edlWarn: EDL mode is for low-level flashing (QFIL/firehose). Leaving it usually requires holding the power button for ~10–20 s. Continue?
adv.title: Advanced
adv.shellHint: Type a command and press Enter. Output appears here.
adv.sideloadHint: Boot recovery → “Apply update from ADB”. The device must show up in Sideload mode.
log.title: Operation log
common.needAdb: This feature requires a device in ADB or Recovery (with ADB) mode.
apps.menuHint: ⋮ next to an app = actions menu
apps.unsupported: command not supported on this Android (SDK {sdk})
apps.confirm.uninstallFull: Completely uninstall the selected apps (pm uninstall)? User apps will be removed TOGETHER WITH THEIR DATA.
apps.fullSystemWarn: The selection contains system apps — a full uninstall without root usually fails (DELETE_FAILED_INTERNAL_ERROR). Use “Uninstall for user 0” for them.
apps.load.details: Reading names and icons from APK files…
apps.load.error: Failed to load the list — see the log
mirror.title: Screenshot & mirroring
mirror.needAdb: Mirroring and screenshots require a device in ADB mode (Android booted).
mirror.missing: scrcpy was not found on this system.
mirror.downloadHint: The app will download the latest release from GitHub (Genymobile/scrcpy) into its own %APPDATA% folder — no installer, no admin rights.
mirror.installHint: Install scrcpy from your distribution's repository
mirror.running: Mirroring runs in a separate window
mirror.controlsHint: In the scrcpy window: mouse = touch, keyboard = typing, right click = Back, middle click = Home, Alt+F = fullscreen, Alt+O = turn device screen off.
drivers.title: Drivers & USB permissions
drivers.subWin: Windows: detects INF packages and devices without a driver, silent install (pnputil / msiexec).
drivers.subLinux: Linux: udev rules (pkexec / sudo) and USB device access.
drivers.allGood: All good - no missing drivers or permissions.
drivers.uacHint: Installation needs a UAC (administrator) confirmation. INF packages install silently via pnputil; .exe installers without silent arguments show their own window.
drivers.udevHint: Rules from M0Rf30/android-udev-rules (validated: no RUN/PROGRAM commands), built-in fallback. Written to /etc/udev/rules.d via pkexec (Polkit dialog) or sudo. Replug the device afterwards.
drivers.pwText: No Polkit agent - enter your user password to install the rules via sudo. The password is never stored or logged.
vendors.title: Vendor tools
sam.notSamsung: The connected device is not a Samsung - some fields may be empty.
sam.dlNoDriver: No driver/permission - install Samsung USB Driver (Windows) or udev rules (Linux).
sam.dlHow1: 2019+ devices: power off, hold Vol Up + Vol Down and plug the USB cable into the PC.
sam.dlHow2: Older with Bixby: Vol Down + Bixby + Power. Older with Home: Vol Down + Home + Power.
sam.dlHow3: On the warning screen press Vol Up (Continue).
sam.dlHow4: From a running system: Power tab → Download Mode (ADB).
sam.lokeNote: USB detection (VID:PID) without sending the ODIN/LOKE handshake - the port stays free for Odin/Heimdall.
xi.needFastboot: Connect the Xiaomi in Fastboot mode (Vol Down + Power) - ARB is read automatically.
xi.vNoArb: Bootloader reports no ARB - no rollback protection (or not a Xiaomi).
xi.vZero: ARB 0 - older versions can be flashed.
xi.vActive: ARB ACTIVE - DO NOT FLASH OLDER FIRMWARE! Compare with a ROM below.
xi.vBrick: BRICK RISK: firmware ARB {fw} < device ARB {dev} - DO NOT FLASH!
xi.vFwNoCheck: The firmware script has no CURRENT_ANTI_VER - check manually.
xi.edlHow1: Entering EDL: Power tab → EDL (needs ADB/unlocked BL), test point or an EDL cable.
xi.edlHow2: Port 9008 leaves the mode after ~10-60 s of inactivity - start the flasher right away.
xi.edlHow3: Newer Xiaomi models require an authorized EDL account (Mi Auth).
xi.edlNote: USB detection without sending Sahara packets - the port stays free for QFIL / Mi Flash / edl.
moto.title: Motorola firmware flasher (flashfile.xml)
moto.hint: Pick an extracted Motorola firmware (folder with flashfile.xml or servicefile.xml and .img/.bin images). Steps are parsed and shown before flashing.
moto.needFastboot: Connect the Motorola in Fastboot mode (Vol Down + Power).
moto.confirmText: Steps run one by one via fastboot. Do not unplug the cable until finished.
moto.confirmWipe: ⚠ The firmware erases userdata - ALL USER DATA WILL BE WIPED.
moto.safety: Cancelling only works between steps (never during a partition write). A flash/erase error stops the process.
diag.title: Hardware diagnostics
diag.idle: Click Start to read the battery and sensors live.
diag.noThermal: No readable thermal_zone entries (root required on this device).
diag.note: sysfs units differ between vendors - values are normalized (µV→mV, µA→mA, m°C→°C).
logcat.kernelHint: Kernel buffer (dmesg) - needs root on most devices
logcat.tail: How many recent lines to fetch on start
logcat.export: Export the full buffer to a file
logcat.regexPh: Regex filter (tag or message), e.g. camera|SurfaceFlinger
logcat.idle: Click Start - filtering runs in Rust, the GUI only receives matching lines.
odin.repartWarn: RE-PARTITION overwrites the partition table from the PIT file. A wrong PIT = brick. Use only a verified PIT for this exact model.
odin.needHeimdall: Install Heimdall to flash (PIT read works without it).
odin.confirmText: Flashing via Heimdall. Do not unplug the cable or power off until finished. Wrong firmware or interruption can brick the device.
odin.confirmRepart: ⚠ RE-PARTITION enabled - the partition table will be overwritten from the PIT.
odin.confirmData: ⚠ The set contains CSC/USERDATA - user data may be wiped.
odin.engineNote: Detection and PIT read are native (USB/LOKE). The firmware write itself is done by the proven open-source Heimdall engine - deliberately, because a wrong PIT write can brick the device.
ent.title: Enterprise & Provisioning
ent.sub: Fleet provisioning: Zero-Touch Setup (ADB), OEM commands (Fastboot), MTP init.
ent.fbConfirm: This fastboot command may be irreversible (unlock = wipe, erase = partition data loss). Continue?
ent.mdmUrl: Open URL in browser (e.g. MDM profile)
ent.localeRootHint: Changing persist.sys.locale needs root; without root use “Language settings”.
ent.needFastboot: Connect the device in Fastboot mode.
ent.mtpNote: Standard Android MTP usually can't reboot to a mode - the reliable way is a key combo. Below is a best-effort PTP ResetDevice.
ent.outputHint: Output of executed commands appears here.
dt.title: APK Inspector & DevTools
dt.subtitle: Decompile • edit manifest & resources • build • sign • install
dt.fwHint: Manually import framework-res.apk / a vendor framework (when the source device isn't at hand)
dt.setupHint: Missing tools (apktool, uber-apk-signer and, if needed, Java JRE 21) are downloaded automatically from official GitHub releases and verified with SHA-256 - on first use or with the button above.
dt.noJavaPlatform: No Java 8+ and no JRE package available for this platform - install Java (e.g. Temurin 21) manually.
dt.needAdb: Select a device in ADB mode (Android booted, USB debugging) to pull an installed app.
dt.fileHint: Supported: single .apk, .apks/.xapk bundles, a folder with base.apk + split_*.apk (e.g. from “Extract APK”).
dt.decompileHint: Pull → apktool d into a workspace. Then edit the manifest and resources below.
dt.autoHint: Pull from device → Decompile → Edit → Build → Sign → Install. Any failing step stops the chain with a readable error.
dt.cloneHint: The clone installs next to the original. Provider authorities, custom permissions and taskAffinity are rewritten too. Apps that check their own signature/package may misbehave.
dt.cloneSplit: Cloning is not available for split apps (multiple APK files) - renaming would require rebuilding every part.
dt.badPkg: Invalid package name (e.g. com.company.app.clone - at least 2 segments, letters/digits/_) or same as the original.
dt.noChanges: No manifest changes for the selected options.
dt.uninstallMsg: The rebuilt APK has a different signature than the original, so Android won't allow an update. Uninstalling DELETES this app's data on the device. Lossless alternative: cloning.
dt.deleteMsg: Decoded files, replaced resources and built APKs of this workspace will be removed from disk.
dt.label: Name
dt.installNeedsAdb: Installing requires a device in ADB mode - without it the APK is only built (and saved if you pick a folder).
dt.exportNone: (optional - a copy always stays in the workspace)
dt.signNote: Signature: local debug key (RSA 2048, generated once) - later builds install as updates.
dt.pickFile: Pick a file in the tree to preview it.
dt.noPreview: No preview for this file type.
dt.ninePatchNote: 9-patch: the new image needs a 1px border with black markers, otherwise the build fails.
dt.resNote: Images are replaced with a file of the same format (PNG/JPG/WEBP…); files in assets/ with any file. Changes go into the APK on the next build.
dt.seeLog: Full tool output is in the log (source: apk).
dt.legal: Developer tool: modifies APK structure (flags, package name, resources). No code, licence or protection tampering - use for your own or permitted apps.
wifi.title: Connect over Wi-Fi
wifi.subtitle: Wireless ADB - pairing code (Android 11+) or TCP/IP (Android 10 and older)
wifi.pairHow: On the device: Developer options → Wireless debugging → “Pair device with pairing code”. Copy the IP address, port and 6-digit code from the popup. The computer and the device must be on the same network.
wifi.connectHow: The device was already paired with this computer: enter the IP address and port from the main “Wireless debugging” screen (“IP address & Port”).
wifi.connectPortHint: Empty = detected automatically (mDNS). Note: the connect port differs from the pairing port.
wifi.connectPortHint2: The port changes every time Wireless debugging is turned on.
wifi.tcpHow: For devices connected by cable (including Android 10 and older): the tool reads the device IP address, switches adbd to TCP/IP mode and connects wirelessly. The device must be on the same Wi-Fi/Ethernet network as the computer.
wifi.noUsb: No ADB device connected over USB. Connect a device with USB debugging enabled and accept the computer's key.
wifi.unplug: You can unplug the USB cable now
wifi.needAuth: Accept “Allow debugging?” on the device screen - until then the device shows as “Unauthorized”.
wifi.uiTimeout: No response from adb in a reasonable time - check the network and try again.
wifi.offlineHint: Wi-Fi connection lost (device asleep, network change or wireless debugging turned off). Disconnect and connect again.
pull.ntfsHint: Characters not allowed on NTFS/FAT32/exFAT (: * ? " < > | \) become _, no trailing dot/space and no names like CON/NUL. Recommended when saving to a USB stick, external drive or Windows partition.
pull.ntfsForced: Always on in Windows - the system can't store such names.
pull.rootDenied: su denied – allow in Magisk and click
pull.rootHintOn: Scan and copy via su: access to /data/data, Android/data and protected files. /data was added to the tree.
pull.rootHintDenied: su is present but denied access. Allow the Shell app in Magisk/KernelSU and click the button at the top.
pull.rootHintOff: No root - everything ADB can access is copied (Android/data is not accessible on Android 11+).
backup.title: Contacts & SMS backup
backup.subtitle: Companion app (Drapco Backup Agent) – works on any Android 5.0+, no root
backup.how: The tool installs a small companion app on the device and opens it on screen. After you allow the permissions and tap “Make backup”, contacts (.vcf) and SMS (.xml, SMS Backup & Restore compatible) are pulled to the computer automatically.
backup.privacy: After pulling, the files are deleted from the device and the companion app is uninstalled – also on error or cancel. Data never leaves the USB cable.
backup.step.deploy: Installing the companion app (adb install, manually from Download if blocked)
backup.step.launch: Opening it on the device screen
backup.step.wait: Waiting for consent and the backup button
backup.step.cleanup: Cleaning up and uninstalling the app
backup.modal1: Unlock the device screen – “Drapco Backup Agent” is already open.
backup.modal2: Allow Contacts and SMS access in the system dialogs.
backup.modal3: Tap “Make backup” on the phone – files are pulled automatically.
backup.failedNote: The companion app was uninstalled and temporary files were removed from the device.
backup.xiaomiNote: Xiaomi/Redmi/POCO: enable “Install via USB” in Developer options. If the install is blocked, the tool sends Agent.apk to Download for manual installation.
backup.step.push: Sending the backup to the device (adb push)
backup.step.waitRestore: Restoring on the device and tapping “Done”
backup.manual.title: USB installation blocked
backup.manual.text: USB installation is blocked. The file was sent to the Download folder. Open the file manager on the phone, install Agent.apk manually and click Done.
backup.manual.tip2: If asked, allow that app to install unknown apps.
backup.manual.tip3: Play Protect may warn about an unknown app – choose “Install anyway”. The agent and the file are removed afterwards.
backup.manual.pending: The agent is not installed yet – finish the installation on the device and click Done again.
backup.manual.auto: Installation is detected automatically every 2 s
restore.how: Choose the backup folder (contacts.vcf and/or sms.xml – e.g. a folder created by “Backup”). The tool sends the files to Download/Restore on the device and starts the helper app in restore mode.
restore.smsNote: To restore SMS the helper app must briefly become the default SMS app (an Android requirement). When finished, switch back to your SMS app – the computer checks this and restores it itself if needed.
restore.modalTitle: Restore the data on the device
restore.modal1: Unlock the screen – “Drapco Backup Agent” is open in restore mode.
restore.modal2: “Restore contacts” – the Contacts app imports the file (confirm the import if asked).
restore.modal3: “Restore SMS” – allow the agent to be the default SMS app temporarily and wait until it finishes.
restore.modal4: “Restore default SMS app” – pick your usual app (e.g. Google / Samsung Messages), then “Done”.
restore.failedNote: The helper app was uninstalled and the uploaded files were removed from the device.
restore.cancelled: Restore cancelled – files removed, helper app uninstalled
restore.defaultBad: Check the default SMS app: Settings → Apps → Default apps → SMS
restore.incoming: SMS received during the restore were saved
restore.restricted: Android 13+: if “Restricted setting” appears when changing the SMS app, open the agent's App info → ⋮ → “Allow restricted settings”.
odin.usbBusy: flashing in progress – USB reserved for Heimdall
update.title: New version available
update.upToDateText: ADB Service Tool is up to date.
update.restarting: Done – starting the new version, the app will close in a moment.
update.pkgReady: Package downloaded and verified (SHA-256). Install it with the command or the button below.
update.devBuild: Development build – installing updates is disabled.
update.noManifest: The release has no latest.json – download the new version from the release page.
update.noAsset: No file for this installation type – download the new version from the release page.
sei.title: Smart EI
sei.subtitle: Smart Export Import – move to a new phone step by step
sei.conn.title: Connection
sei.conn.adbDesc: The agent installs automatically; fastest verified transfers, settings and a home screen screenshot.
sei.conn.wifiDesc: No USB debugging needed: the phone pairs with this computer over the local network using a QR code and PIN.
sei.needAdb: Connect a phone with USB debugging (ADB) or choose “Connect without ADB”.
sei.noLan: No local network connection found – connect the computer to the same Wi-Fi/LAN as the phone.
sei.mod.apks: Also export APK files of apps from outside Google Play (own APKs)
sei.mod.settingsHint: Only portable, safe settings: screen timeout, font size, auto-rotate, dark mode, 24-hour clock and volumes.
sei.destHint: A SmartEI_<Model>_<Date> folder will be created inside. Select an existing SmartEI_ folder to resume an interrupted backup.
sei.noManifest: This folder does not contain a Smart EI backup (manifest.json).
sei.incomplete: Incomplete backup (interrupted export) – whatever it contains can be restored.
sei.limit1: Icon layout and widgets cannot be moved between brands (every launcher stores them differently) – Smart EI saves a home screen screenshot so you can arrange them again easily.
sei.limit2: Google Play apps are installed fresh from the store (latest version, your Google account) – Android requires you to tap “Install” yourself; Smart EI opens them one after another.
sei.limit3: WhatsApp chats are restored by WhatsApp itself (its Google Drive backup) – Smart EI moves the WhatsApp photos and media.
sei.limit4: Nothing leaves your local network: the Wi-Fi bridge runs only during the transfer and is protected by a PIN and a one-time session token.
sei.adb.deploy: Installing the agent on the phone…
sei.adb.wait: Unlock the phone – the agent connects to the computer over USB.
sei.wifi.step1Text: If the Drapco agent is not on the phone yet: copy Agent.apk to the phone, or scan the QR code to download it over Wi-Fi, and install it.
sei.wifi.apkQr: QR code to download the APK over Wi-Fi
sei.wifi.step2Text: Scan this code with the phone camera and tap “Drapco Agent”, or open the agent and type the address and PIN:
sei.wifi.step3Text: After pairing a summary appears here; the data then travels directly over Wi-Fi with size verification.
sei.wifi.firewall: Windows: if the phone cannot connect, allow ADB Service Tool in Windows Defender Firewall (private networks).
sei.review.title: Summary
sei.review.notEnough: Not enough disk space – free up space or choose another folder.
sei.review.crossVendor: Different manufacturer – apps of the source phone's manufacturer are unchecked (recommended).
sei.review.phoneNotEnough: Not enough free space on the phone for the selected files.
sei.review.phoneExport: After clicking Start, tap “Start export” on the phone.
sei.review.phoneImport: After clicking Start, tap “Start import” on the phone.
sei.resume: Resume: the selected folder already contains a Smart EI backup – files already copied are skipped.
sei.apps.title: Apps
sei.stage.finish: Almost done – tap Finish on the phone.
sei.queue.title: Google Play
sei.queue.hint: Tap “Install” in Google Play on the phone. The next app opens automatically as soon as the installation is detected.
sei.cancelled: Cancelled – files already saved stay in place, you can resume.
